headline: How Sparify Helped Motorcycle Enthusiasts Shop Smarter and Boosted Revenue by 51%
overview:
Sparify is a leading online destination for motorcycle performance parts and accessories, trusted by over 70,000 bikers. The platform offers a wide range of products, from helmets and riding gear to bike-specific parts, with a focus on quality, reliability and rider confidence.

To optimize the mobile shopping journey, Sparify partnered with ConvertPolo to revamp the Product Detail Pages (PDPs), introduce dynamic shipping messaging, and implement urgency-driven cart nudges.
challenge: Sparify's shoppers faced friction at multiple points in the purchase journey. On product pages, key details like specifications, sizing, safety certifications and product value were hard to find. The PDP layouts did not encourage exploration of images, coupons or social proof. Cart abandonment was elevated because the experience lacked urgency cues to prompt checkout and the absence of dynamic shipping information created uncertainty around delivery timelines. These issues limited conversions across the funnel.
solutions: Redesigned the helmet PDP to highlight specifications, safety certifications, size guides and images, enabling more informed product evaluation.
Added dynamic, inventory-driven shipping messages to show real-time delivery timelines, which reduced purchase uncertainty.
Implemented FOMO-based cart nudges like “Limited stock available” to encourage checkout and lower abandonment.
Improved engagement with coupon boxes and PDP thumbnails, making offers and product details easier to explore.

experiments.title: Helmet PDP Revamp
experiments.problem: Users struggled to evaluate helmets due to unorganized product information, unclear specifications, missing safety certifications, and poorly structured visuals, which slowed decision-making.
experiments.hypothesis: If we redesign the helmet PDP with a clear layout, upfront shipping info, social proof, easy payment options, size information and prominent visual, users will make faster, more confident decisions.
experiments.conclusion: By reorganizing helmet pages with clear specs, safety info, and visuals, users evaluated products faster and added more items to their carts.

experiments.title: Cart Nudge – FOMO Messaging
experiments.problem: Users often left the cart without completing checkout because the page didn't highlight limited stock or urgency.
experiments.hypothesis: If we introduce FOMO-based nudges like “Limited stock available” or “Buy now before it sells out,” users will feel a stronger sense of urgency.
experiments.conclusion: Introducing urgency-focused nudges prompted users to act quickly, leading to higher checkout completion and increased revenue.

experiments.title: Dynamic Shipping Messaging
experiments.problem: Users lacked a clear perception of the delivery date, with no real-time shipping information, which led to slowed purchase decisions.
experiments.hypothesis: If we show inventory-based dynamic shipping timelines on PDPs, users will understand fulfillment expectations, feel more confident, and be more likely to proceed with Add to Cart actions.
experiments.conclusion: Displaying real-time, inventory-based delivery timelines reduced uncertainty, which gave users confidence to add products to their carts.

experiments.title: Performance Parts PDP Revamp
experiments.problem: Performance parts PDPs under-communicated product value, trust signals, offers and USPs.
experiments.hypothesis: If we improve visual hierarchy, surface key USPs, enhance image prominence, highlight offers, and add social proof elements, users will better understand value and engage more.
experiments.conclusion: Improving visual hierarchy, highlighting key offers, and adding social proof helped users understand the product's value and engage more with PDP features.

overallImpact: By addressing friction at key points in the mobile journey, Sparify created a smoother, more confident, and intent-driven shopping experience. PDP revamps, dynamic shipping messaging, and FOMO-based cart nudges worked together to help users evaluate products faster, trust delivery timelines and act decisively at checkout.

headline: How ConvertPolo increased Theater.xyz's Add-to-Cart by over 42%
overview:
Theater.xyz is an innovative fashion brand, specializing in a diverse range of apparel and accessories for both men and women. Their product lineup includes footwear, socks, bags, jewelry and more, catering to a wide audience seeking stylish and affordable fashion options.

ConvertPolo's in-depth behavioral analysis and heuristic evaluation identified a lack of trust, relevance, and product discoverability as key barriers, resulting in a +42% increase in Add-to-Cart actions, demonstrating the success of the solution.
challenge: Theatre.xyz aimed to boost its revenue, but the website was experiencing low transaction conversion rates despite a steady influx of visitors. Data showed that 30% of users were abandoning their journey before viewing products, and 92.4% were leaving before adding a product to the cart.
solutions: Introduced a sticky filter and sort function on mobile PLPs to keep refinement controls accessible at all times, helping users quickly narrow down relevant products and improve product discovery.
Added meta suggestions on the Product Display Page to surface related options and contextual cues, enabling users to explore alternatives seamlessly and increasing engagement during browsing.
Enhanced the add-to-cart action with social proof and FOMO-based messaging to reduce hesitation, build trust, and prompt faster purchase decisions on mobile.

experiments.title: Add Sticky Filter & Sort Function
experiments.problem: Visitors were not finding relevant products to purchase at the right stage of their journey on the website
experiments.hypothesis: Introducing a sticky filter and sort function would enhance product discovery by enabling users to easily navigate and refine their options. This improvement would help users feel more confident and informed in their product choices.
experiments.conclusion: Users found it easier to navigate and discover products that matched their interests, resulting in smoother browsing experiences and higher engagement across the homepage.

experiments.title: Meta Suggestions on Product Display Page
experiments.problem: Lack of relevance and discoverability while browsing.
experiments.hypothesis: If meta suggestions are added, it improves discoverability by offering additional context or related options beyond the immediate product being viewed.
experiments.conclusion: Users were more likely to explore additional options tailored to their interests, resulting in increased engagement across the platform

stats.label: Rise in Add to Cart Conversions

experiments.title: Enhance Add-to-Cart Action
experiments.problem: Lack of trust and uncertainty on the visitor's part can be detrimental to cart health.
experiments.hypothesis: If social proof messages based on FOMO (Fear of Missing Out), Trust, and aggravated FOMO are provided, it would motivate users to view products and add them to their carts.
experiments.conclusion: By leveraging psychological triggers like urgency and scarcity, users were compelled to take immediate action to avoid missing out on desirable opportunities. Users became more motivated to secure products before they were perceived to be unavailable.

overallImpact: By systematically addressing two different problem statements that led to poor performance of the E-commerce Conversion Rate, our team was able to achieve a notable improvement with a structured and comprehensive strategy. This thorough methodology ensured that potential obstacles were identified and resolved, creating a clear path to measurable success.

headline: Theater Achieves 38% Growth in Revenue per Visitor Through Mobile Experience Redesign
overview:
Theater.xyz is a digital-first fashion and lifestyle brand offering western apparel and accessories across categories such as footwear, stockings, perfumes, bags, and men's essentials. With a mobile-heavy audience, the brand's growth depended on making product discovery and evaluation seamless on smaller screens.

Theater partnered with ConvertPolo to reduce decision friction throughout the mobile journey, to achieve higher conversions and revenue. The focus was on enhancing product pages to reduce decision friction, introducing intuitive guidance tools such as size information and creating engaging discovery elements to help shoppers find their ideal products faster.
challenge:
Theater's mobile shopping journey faced decision friction at key moments in the funnel.

Product clarity gaps: Important details such as material, fit, and quality benefits were not structured to communicate value fast and build confidence.

Sizing uncertainty: High-fit products lacked easily accessible size guidance, leading to hesitation and delayed purchase decisions.

Discovery limitations: In categories like perfumes, static browsing without personalization left users unsure about what suited them, lowering add-to-cart intent.
solutions: The PDP was restructured to highlight clear, benefit-led details such as fabric, comfort, and durability, helping users evaluate products faster and purchase with greater confidence.
A prominent size guide trigger was introduced, opening a quick-access overlay with sizing information to reduce fit uncertainty without disrupting the buying flow.
A 5-step interactive quiz was added above the perfume listings to capture user preferences and guide shoppers toward personalized fragrance recommendations.

experiments.title: Men's Socks PDP Enhancement
experiments.problem: The socks PDP showed only basic information, with no structured highlights for fabric, comfort, durability or usage. Key benefits were not easily scannable.
experiments.hypothesis: If we present concise, benefit-led bullet points covering material, comfort features, and durability, users will better understand the product and generate higher revenue per visitor.
experiments.conclusion: Clearer benefit communication improved evaluation speed and purchase confidence.

experiments.title: Size Guide Popup Introduction
experiments.problem: The mobile PDP lacked an easily accessible size guide, creating uncertainty for high-fit products and increasing hesitation at checkout.
experiments.hypothesis: If we add a prominent “Size Guide” trigger with an instant popup overlay, users will gain fit clarity without leaving the PDP, leading to higher completed orders.
experiments.conclusion: Providing sizing clarity at the moment of intent reduced friction and improved conversions.

experiments.title: Perfume Discovery Quiz Launch
experiments.problem: The perfume PLP relied on static listings without guidance, leaving users unsure which fragrance suited them and lowering add-to-cart rates.
experiments.hypothesis: If we introduce a short, interactive quiz that captures preferences and recommends tailored perfumes, users will feel more confident selecting a product and add more items to cart.
experiments.conclusion: Guided discovery reduced decision fatigue and strengthened purchase intent.

overallImpact: By addressing decision friction at multiple stages of the mobile funnel, Theater transformed key evaluation and discovery moments into conversion drivers. Clearer PDP communication improved product understanding, sizing guidance reduced purchase hesitation, and guided perfume discovery helped users choose with confidence.

headline: TryEvolv improved its website experience and boosted e-commerce conversion by 200%
overview:
TryEvolv is a mobile-first e-commerce platform focused on helping users discover and purchase products quickly and confidently. Users often browse multiple categories and products, but friction in navigation, engagement, and add-to-cart actions slows their journey.

ConvertPolo partnered with TryEvolv to streamline early and mid-funnel interactions by reducing effort, increasing visibility of key information and reinforcing purchase confidence on mobile.
challenge: On the homepage, the traditional hamburger menu made category discovery difficult, leading to fewer category clicks and exploration. On product pages, users hesitated to purchase due to hidden product benefits and a non-intuitive add-to-cart process. Engagement on product detail pages was low, with static product information failing to capture attention or prompt action. Across these stages, friction increased cognitive load and delayed purchase decisions.
solutions: Introduced visible category tags directly below the top banner to make navigation immediate and intuitive.
Combined customer reviews with a sticky add-to-cart button to provide trust signals and simplify purchase actions.
Made product benefits interactive and implemented a sticky add-to-cart button across the product page.

experiments.title: Category Tags on Homepage
experiments.problem: The control version of the homepage used a traditional design with a hamburger menu for category navigation. While functional, this design didn't effectively highlight products or encourage further exploration.
experiments.hypothesis: If category tags are placed directly below the top banner, it will be easy for users to identify and access the product categories they were most interested in.
experiments.conclusion: This new layout made it easy for users to identify and access the product categories they were most interested in.

experiments.title: Review Highlight & Sticky Add to Cart
experiments.problem: The add-to-cart process was not intuitive and hence the drop-off was high. Despite spending considerable time exploring the site and actively scrolling through content, visitors showed minimal engagement with call-to-action buttons.
experiments.hypothesis: Strategic placement of customer reviews combined with a sticky add-to-cart button would increase purchase motivation by providing immediate access to social proof and simplified purchase actions.
experiments.conclusion: The combination of visible reviews and an ever-present add-to-cart button built instant trust and reduced friction, motivating users to make quicker purchase decisions.

experiments.title: Interactive Product Benefits & Sticky Add-to-Cart Button
experiments.problem: Engagement on the product display page was low due to features that did not encourage interaction on the page.
experiments.hypothesis: Making the product benefits interactive and the add-to-cart CTA button sticky reduces the cognitive dissonance and increases interactiveness thereby increasing revenue through increased engagement.
experiments.conclusion: Making the product details interactive kept users engaged and encouraged them to take action faster, which led to more clicks and higher purchases.

overallImpact: Through ConvertPolo's strategic direction and a data-driven approach to experimentation, TryEvolv achieved a 200% increase in e-commerce conversions. The team successfully addressed key challenges by creating a more intuitive, trust-building user experience. For a premium product with a complex value proposition, simplifying the purchase journey while reinforcing credibility proved critical to driving results.

headline: How iTokri Increased Add-to-Cart by 221% Through UX Refinement on Mobile
overview:
iTokri is a purpose-driven online platform that curates and sells handcrafted products made by Indian artisans. With a focus on ethical sourcing and heritage-rich craftsmanship, it caters to customers globally looking for unique Indian fabrics, apparel, and décor.

To improve the buyer journey and boost conversions, iTokri partnered with ConvertPolo to run UX-driven experiments targeting discovery, comparison shopping, and checkout confidence. The result was a remarkable +221% uplift in Add-to-Cart actions, a +36.76% improvement in conversion rate, and a measurable increase in bottom-funnel efficiency.
challenge: While the brand had high intent traffic and a strong catalog, user behavior data revealed friction at critical stages, especially during filtering, product revisits, and checkout. Filters were hard to access, users couldn't easily return to previously viewed items, product pages added unnecessary navigation steps, and the cart lacked trust signals. These friction points limited conversion potential.
solutions: Introduced a “Recently Viewed Items” section to support product recall and comparison.
Enabled quick view and direct Add-to-Cart on product listing pages to reduce browsing friction.
Added trust-building elements to the cart to reduce hesitation at checkout.

experiments.title: Recently Viewed Items Chiplet
experiments.problem: Users had no way to return to previously viewed products, making it hard to compare items or resume a purchase decision. This affected users who browsed multiple items before deciding.
experiments.hypothesis: A “Recently Viewed Items” Chiplet was added across major pages, helping users re-access previously explored products. This supported decision-making, especially for hesitant or returning users.
experiments.conclusion: Guided search prompts reduced uncertainty and encouraged users to explore more confidently.

experiments.title: Quick View & Add to Cart on PLP
experiments.problem: Users had to load individual Product Detail Pages (PDP) just to view details or add items to their cart. This slowed down the decision process and led to fatigue, especially during comparison shopping.
experiments.hypothesis: Quick View modals and Add to Cart buttons were implemented directly on the Product Listing Page (PLP), allowing users to interact with product details and add items to cart without page reloads.
experiments.conclusion: Reduced steps to purchase and enabled fast decisions, especially on mobile.

stats.label: Rise in ATC Clicks on PLP

experiments.title: Cart Page Optimization
experiments.problem: The cart lacked persuasive elements such as trust badges, return policies, and customer reviews. This eroded confidence and increased drop-offs, particularly for new or cautious users.
experiments.hypothesis: Added key Trust Signals like secure payment indicators, verified customer reviews, USPs like “Easy Returns” and “Free Shipping”
experiments.conclusion: Reduced steps to purchase and enabled fast decisions, especially on mobile.

overallImpact: These enhancements directly tackled mid- to bottom-funnel drop-offs and significantly improved the shopper's ability to browse, compare, and convert.

impactStats.label: Rise in Add to Cart Actions

headline: How iTokri Achieved 98% Growth in Revenue with UX Enhancements
overview:
iTokri is an e-commerce platform that offers authentic Indian handicrafts, textiles, and accessories sourced directly from artisans. Its mission is to create meaningful bridges between rural craftsmanship and global consumers. With a vast catalog and an artisan-first approach, iTokri aims to combine storytelling with sustainable retail.

They partnered with ConvertPolo to improve their eCommerce experience, aiming to increase revenue and lift conversion rates through a series of UX-focused experiments. These enhancements resulted in a 98% increase in revenue, a 15% rise in Add-to-Cart actions, and a 42% uplift in conversion rate.
challenge: Despite a strong product catalog and customer loyalty, iTokri's digital storefront was facing barriers in user navigation and product engagement. Categories were difficult to find, the mobile navigation lacked visual clarity, the search function failed to support product discovery, and the Product Detail Pages (PDPs) lacked persuasive design. These shortcomings created friction at multiple stages of the user journey, limiting conversion rates and revenue potential.
solutions: Introduced prominent, multi-tile category sections on the homepage to reduce scroll friction and improve product visibility.

Redesigned the mobile PDP with trust signals, sticky CTAs, and optimized galleries for better persuasion and purchase intent

headline: MyRivaaz Increased Add-to-Cart Rate by 100.79% Through Better Navigation and Collection Discovery
overview:
MyRivaaz is an online Indian and Pakistani jewelry store based in Maryland, USA, offering bridal, festive, and occasion-based jewelry across categories such as necklaces, earrings, bangles, rings, maang tikkas, and wedding sets.

MyRivaaz partnered with ConvertPolo to improve the mobile shopping experience by reducing discovery friction and making key collections easier to access. The focus was on helping shoppers explore products more intuitively while building confidence throughout the browsing journey.
challenge:
The mobile experience created friction across key browsing and discovery touchpoints.

Navigation lacked context: The hamburger menu functioned as a text-heavy directory and offered limited access to key utilities.

Promotions lacked visibility: Important campaigns and featured collections were not immediately visible.

Discovery lacked inspiration: Generic category icons provided little visual context, making collection exploration less engaging.
solutions: The hamburger menu was redesigned with visual category navigation and quick access to support and account actions.
The hero banner was moved above the fold and static category icons were replaced with an interactive collection discovery section.
The navigation experience was enhanced with richer visual cues and improved access to key utility actions.

experiments.conclusion: The visual navigation experience reduced discovery friction and encouraged more shoppers to progress toward purchase.

experiments.title: Utility-First Navigation Optimization
experiments.problem: The existing navigation relied heavily on text and offered limited visual guidance. Key support and account actions were not easily accessible, creating friction during product discovery.
experiments.hypothesis: If the hamburger menu is redesigned with visual category cues and prominent utility actions, shoppers will navigate more confidently and progress further toward purchase.
experiments.conclusion: Improved navigation clarity helped shoppers discover products faster and take action with greater confidence.

overallImpact: By improving collection discovery and simplifying navigation, MyRivaaz transformed key browsing touchpoints into stronger purchase pathways. headline: How Kisah Drove 119% Higher Revenue and 120% Conversion Growth Through Mobile Experience Optimization
overview:
Kisah is a contemporary ethnic menswear brand known for its refined silhouettes, rich fabrics, and modern interpretations of traditional Indian wear. With a strong presence in kurtas, festive wear, and occasion-led collections, the brand appeals to style-conscious shoppers seeking elegance without compromise.

To elevate the mobile shopping journey, Kisah partnered with ConvertPolo to increase personalization, strengthen product discovery and unify the PDP experience. The optimization focused on reducing effort across the funnel for a smoother user journey.
challenge: Kisah was driving quality mobile traffic, but the experience wasn't sustaining buying momentum. Shoppers had to repeatedly reselect sizes while browsing, PLPs didn't actively guide discovery or encourage deeper exploration and PDPs lacked a clear structure to move users toward the final Add to Cart action. These small but frequent interruptions increased effort at every step.
solutions: Introduced a persistent preferred-size selection early in the journey, allowing users to set their size once and carry it seamlessly across collections and product pages.
Revamped the mobile PLP by bringing together proven UX improvements into a single, cohesive layout that enhanced product visibility through filters and discovery cues.
Optimized the mobile PDP to show critical product information instantly, reducing evaluation time and helping users make faster, more confident purchase decisions.

experiments.title: Personalized Sizing throughout the journey
experiments.problem: Users had to repeatedly select their size while browsing collections and PDPs, creating friction, slowing product discovery, and disrupting the shopping flow, especially in size-sensitive categories.
experiments.hypothesis: If users can select their preferred size upfront and have it persist across the site, we can reduce friction, speed up discovery, and increase relevant product views, Add to Cart actions and conversions.
experiments.conclusion: The persistent size-selection experience removed repeated friction, accelerated product discovery and delivered substantial improvements.

stats.label: Increase in Preferred Size Popup Interaction

experiments.title: PLP Revamp
experiments.problem: The PLP has issues of fragmented UX such as limited visibility, unclear hierarchy, and weak engagement, reducing product discovery and impacting add-to-cart and conversions.
experiments.hypothesis: If we combine proven improvements into a single, cohesive PLP redesign, we can streamline browsing, boost engagement and increase conversions.
experiments.conclusion: A clearer, more cohesive PLP improved browsing momentum and translated into stronger add-to-cart and purchase intent.

experiments.title: PDP Revamp
experiments.problem: Users face difficulty evaluating products on the PDP due to scattered layouts, weak hierarchy and unclear trust cues, which affects confidence and reduces add-to-cart actions.
experiments.hypothesis: By bringing successful elements together into a more cohesive and intuitive PDP experience, users will be able to assess products faster and convert at higher rates.
experiments.conclusion: When product information became immediately visible, users evaluated faster, trusted more, and converted at a much higher rate.

stats.label: More Clicks on Add to Cart

overallImpact: By reducing friction across key moments in the mobile journey, Kisah created a smoother, more intent-driven shopping experience. Size personalization, improved product discovery, and clearer PDP communication worked together to help users browse faster, evaluate confidently, and take action more decisively, resulting in strong gains in engagement, conversions and revenue

headline: How Mobile UX Optimization Helped My Sanskritam Boost Revenue by +115%
overview:
My Sanskritam is a fast-growing ethnic fashion brand offering contemporary Indian wear across categories like kurtas, co-ord sets, festive collections and more. As the brand is renowned for its vibrant aesthetics, meticulous craftsmanship and versatile silhouettes, it attracts shoppers seeking modern Indian fashion with a traditional touch.

The brand attracts high-intent shoppers but the mobile buying journey had several friction points. In order to strengthen the mobile experience, My Sanskritam partnered with ConvertPolo to enhance navigation clarity, improve PLP engagement and introduce value-driven nudges on PDPs.
challenge: While users were browsing the catalog extensively, they often struggled to reach the right categories, evaluate products quickly or feel motivated to complete their purchase. The navigation wasn't intuitive, the PLP didn't highlight product value, and PDPs lacked compelling incentives. These issues slowed exploration, weakened intent, and led to missed revenue opportunities.
solutions: Redesigned the mobile hamburger menu with category visuals, structured hierarchy, clear Best Seller Tags and New Arrival highlights.
Transformed the mobile PLP with visual tags, quick Add-to-Cart actions, collection banners and review cues.
Added a tiered discount wrapper on PDPs to increase purchase motivation and encourage higher-value carts.

experiments.title: Hamburger Navigation Revamp
experiments.problem: Users found the hamburger menu difficult to scan. Categories looked similar, high-intent sections weren't highlighted and key collections were hidden inside the menu.
experiments.hypothesis: Optimizing the mobile hamburger menu with category images and priority highlights (e.g., ‘Best Seller’ and ‘New Arrivals’) will make it easier for users to discover key products.
experiments.conclusion: The redesigned menu surfaced the right collections at the right moment and significantly boosted downstream purchase performance.

stats.label: Rise in purchase Value per visitor

experiments.title: Product Listing Page Enhancement
experiments.problem: Visual Hierarchy was missing from the PLP. Users couldn't easily differentiate products, spot best sellers or take quick shopping actions. All of these limited the engagement.
experiments.hypothesis: If we highlight product value on the mobile PLP using “New In” or “Best Sellers” ribbons, customer reviews, collection banners and prominent “Add to Cart” and “Quick View” buttons, users will evaluate products faster and discover trending items more easily.
experiments.conclusion: The improved PLP made browsing more purposeful and reduced hesitation, resulting in stronger user action and higher revenue contribution.

experiments.title: Tiered Discount Wrapper on PDP
experiments.problem: Users reached PDPs but lacked a compelling incentive to continue. With no value-driven nudge, PDP abandonment stayed extremely high.
experiments.hypothesis: Introducing a tiered discount structure will motivate users to add more products to their cart, reduce product page abandonment and increase average order value by unlocking higher savings.
experiments.conclusion: The tiered incentive successfully nudged users to act, reducing abandonment and driving higher-value carts.

overallImpact: With focused UX improvements across discovery, evaluation, and motivation, My Sanskritam successfully turned browsing friction into smooth and confident shopping behaviour. Each experiment resolved a specific bottleneck and created a more intuitive, conversion-friendly mobile experience.
